subject.title: PR1/5 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw publish and own this separate residual-gap durable-core RFC, or should accepted invariants remain within the existing TaskFlow architecture and documentation?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but source inspection cannot decide whether maintainers want a second public architecture boundary that also gates a larger runtime stack.

options.title: Sponsor and consolidate
options.body: Have the TaskFlow owner approve the useful residual invariants and place them in the canonical TaskFlow architecture, retaining a separate RFC only where a distinct owner boundary is necessary.

options.title: Publish the standalone RFC
options.body: Merge the unlisted proposal pages as a public architecture artifact with a named owner, explicit status, and a maintenance contract relative to TaskFlow.

options.title: Reject the separate boundary
options.body: Close this proposal and reassess the dependent durable-runtime stack against the existing TaskFlow architecture.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and consolidate
recommendation.body: Have the TaskFlow owner approve the useful residual invariants and place them in the canonical TaskFlow architecture, retaining a separate RFC only where a distinct owner boundary is necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current durable parent-job and operator-control architecture appears to originate from their merged TaskFlow work.
